name: Download New Code at Runtime
description:
Adversaries may download and execute dynamic code not included in the original application package after installation. This technique is primarily used to evade static analysis checks and pre-publication scans in official app stores. In some cases, more advanced dynamic or behavioral analysis techniques could detect this behavior. However, in conjunction with [Execution Guardrails](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1627) techniques, detecting malicious code downloaded after installation could be difficult.

On Android, dynamic code could include native code, Dalvik code, or JavaScript code that utilizes Android WebView’s `JavascriptInterface` capability. 

On iOS, dynamic code could be downloaded and executed through 3rd party libraries such as JSPatch. (Citation: FireEye-JSPatch)

references.description: Jing Xie, Zhaofeng Chen, Jimmy Su. (2016, January 27). HOT OR NOT? THE BENEFITS AND RISKS OF IOS REMOTE HOT PATCHING. Retrieved December 9, 2016.

telemetry.name: File Creation
telemetry.description: Creation or overwrite of a file at an observed path.
telemetry.collection_focus: Scope Sysmon FileCreate (11) to the lab directory; retain the process and file path. Differentiate creation/overwrite if the sensor can.

providers.name: Microsoft Sysmon
providers.scope: Windows event-based collection; enable the event types needed below.

providers.name: Linux Audit
providers.scope: Linux alternative for supported system-call and file events; different semantics and fields.

providers.name: Apple Endpoint Security clients
providers.scope: macOS alternative where the subscribed event exists; requires an entitled, approved client, not an iOS collector.

configuration: On a disposable Windows host, review the installed Sysmon schema and current configuration; merge scoped event filters into the existing policy rather than replacing it.
Forward Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational to the lab collector. Preserve event ID, timestamp, computer, process identifiers and the original event.
For Linux or macOS, select the equivalent sensor separately and test its emitted fields; a Windows event ID does not transfer across platforms.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Event filtering and sensor versions change coverage. High-volume image-load and process-access collection needs tuning; endpoint events alone do not establish intent.

telemetry.name: Network Traffic Content
telemetry.description: Packet or decoded application-protocol content visible at a network sensor.
telemetry.collection_focus: Scope approved packet capture/protocol content collection to the lab flow; retain capture provenance and truncation indicators.

providers.name: Zeek
providers.scope: Connection and protocol metadata from traffic visible to the sensor.

providers.name: Suricata EVE
providers.scope: Configured flow, alert, DNS, HTTP, TLS and protocol records.

configuration: Use an authorized lab TAP/SPAN, virtual mirror or gateway interface. Define which traffic crosses it; avoid assuming visibility into every segment.
Enable the required Zeek analyzers or Suricata EVE event types. Export logs with sensor identity, clock synchronization and flow correlation identifiers.
Monitor capture loss, truncation and exporter sampling. Capture payload only with approval and restrictive retention; encryption normally prevents plaintext inspection.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Flows are not packet payloads. NAT, asymmetric routes, encryption, missing mirrors and sampling can hide attribution or content. A destination connection alone does not prove malicious intent.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per source and observation point: connection rate, destination-host/port fan-out, response/failure ratio and previously unseen destinations. Compare equivalent time windows; separate authorized scanners, NAT and sampling effects.

telemetry.name: OS API Execution
telemetry.description: Instrumented operating-system API calls and their return values.
telemetry.collection_focus: Use an approved EDR trace or instrument the owned lab process at selected APIs. Define API name, caller, sanitized arguments and return status.

providers.name: Application audit logs
providers.scope: First-party service events and request/result fields; schema is application-specific.

providers.name: OpenTelemetry-compatible log pipelines
providers.scope: Transport and normalization of emitted records; do not create missing audit instrumentation.

configuration: Enable the application audit category or instrument the owned lab application at the authorization/action boundary.
Define a schema with timestamp, service, actor, object, action, result and correlation ID. Export structured records through an authenticated collector.
Redact secrets and personal content, separate audit from debug logs, set retention and verify delivery during rotation/restart.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Debug output is not necessarily a durable audit trail. Application developers must emit the relevant event; installing a log pipeline does not make an absent event exist.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per application, client and route: request rate, rare actions, failure ratios and unusual state transitions. Version changes, retries, health probes and seasonal load need separate baselines.

strategies.name: Detection of Download New Code at Runtime

analytics.name: Analytic 1677
analytics.guidance: From the defender’s view: an app retrieves opaque code (DEX/SO/JAR/JS) over the network or IPC, writes it into an app-writable path, optionally performs verification-bypass behaviors (reflection, addJavascriptInterface exposure, or execmem friction), and then loads/executes that code via DexClassLoader/PathClassLoader, dlopen, or WebView bridge invocation within a short window. The analytic correlates Network Content → File Creation/Modification → OS API Execution (loader/syscall/SELinux friction) → Module Load (DexClassLoader/dlopen) and, for WebView paths, Application Log signals of JavaScript interface attachment.

tuning.description: Max correlation window between download → write → load (e.g., 10–60s depending on device/workload).
List of MIME types considered ‘code-like’ (octet-stream, zip, java-archive, x-dex, x-sharedlib, javascript).
Regex for app-writable destinations to watch (/data/data/<pkg>/(files|cache)/, /storage/emulated/0/...).
Entropy cutoff to flag likely code blobs (e.g., ≥ 7.2).
CDNs/domains expected for legitimate updates to reduce FPs.
Bundles/libs known to legitimately load from writable paths (dev/test apps).
Names of allowed WebView JS interfaces for the org (e.g., analytics only).
Foreground/background, Work Profile, dev mode to scope alerts.

log_sources.name: NSM:Flow
log_sources.channel: HTTP(S)/QUIC download of executable/opaque content (application/octet-stream, application/zip, application/java-archive, application/x-dex, application/x-sharedlib, text/javascript)

log_sources.name: android:logcat
log_sources.channel: Create/write under /data/data/<pkg>/(files|cache)/ or /storage/emulated/0/ with extension .dex/.jar/.so/.zip/.tmp/.js and elevated entropy

log_sources.name: android:logcat
log_sources.channel: SELinux AVC for execmem/execute_no_trans/mprotect following recent writes by same UID

log_sources.name: android:logcat
log_sources.channel: DexClassLoader|PathClassLoader load from app-writable path OR dlopen of a freshly created .so

analytics.name: Analytic 1678
analytics.guidance: From the defender’s view: a sandboxed app retrieves code-like content (JS/Mach-O/bundles), writes it to container tmp/Caches, performs memory permission changes (RW→RX/RWX) or directly loads via dyld/dlopen from writable paths, sometimes preceded by 3rd-party hotpatch frameworks (e.g., JSPatch-like behavior) or script engine evaluation. The analytic correlates Network Content → File Creation → OS API Execution (memory permission change) → Module Load (dyld/dlopen) and/or Process Access (codesign validation touches), with optional scripting engine events.

tuning.description: Max correlation window between download → write → load (e.g., 15–60s).
MIME list treated as code-like (octet-stream, zip, javascript, x-mach-o).
Regex for app container tmp/Caches writable paths.
Entropy cutoff to flag code blobs (e.g., ≥ 7.3).
Bundles that legitimately do JIT/script eval to reduce RWX noise.
Regex for loads from writable paths only (exclude app bundle).
Foreground/background or Work Profile state to filter noise.

log_sources.name: iOS:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Per-App VPN flow with code-like content types (application/octet-stream, application/zip, text/javascript, application/x-mach-o)

log_sources.name: iOS:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Create/write in /var/mobile/Containers/Data/Application/<GUID>/(tmp|Library/Caches)/ for .js/.bundle/.dylib/.zip with elevated entropy

log_sources.name: iOS:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: mmap/mprotect transitions to PROT_EXEC for pages associated with recently written files

log_sources.name: iOS:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: dlopen/image load from app-writable path (tmp, Caches) outside bundled resources
